question: The __________ is a dark, spherical structure in the cell, surrounded by a __________ membrane with pores for material exchange.
solution:
The correct answer is __**nucleus; double**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **nucleus** is a specialized **cell organelle** that acts as the **control center** of the **eukaryotic cell**, containing the majority of the cell's **genetic material**.
 
• It is characterized by a **spherical** or **oval** shape and was first discovered and described by the scientist **Robert Brown** in **1831**.
 
• The nucleus is enclosed by a **double membrane** known as the **nuclear envelope**. This structure consists of an **inner membrane** and an **outer membrane** separated by the **perinuclear space**. ***Hence, the structure is a nucleus with a double membrane.***
 
• The **nuclear envelope** is not continuous; it is interrupted by numerous **nuclear pores**. These **pores** are critical for the **material exchange**, allowing the regulated movement of **RNA**, **proteins**, and **ribosomal subunits** between the **nucleoplasm** and the **cytoplasm**.
 
• In contrast, a **nucleoid** (mentioned in options 1 and 3) is an irregularly shaped region within **prokaryotic cells** that contains genetic material but **lacks a nuclear membrane** entirely.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure of the Nucleoplasm:**
 
 
• The **nucleoplasm** (also known as nuclear sap) is the **gelatinous substance** within the nucleus that houses the **chromatin** and the **nucleolus**.
 
• **Chromatin** consists of **DNA** and **histone proteins**. During **cell division**, chromatin condenses into highly organized structures called **chromosomes**.
 
 
 
• **The Nucleolus:**
 
 
• The **nucleolus** is a distinct, non-membrane-bound dense structure found inside the nucleus. It is the primary site for **ribosomal RNA (rRNA)** synthesis and the assembly of **ribosomes**.
 
• Cells that are actively involved in **protein synthesis** usually possess larger and more numerous **nucleoli**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Vacuoles:**
 
 
• A **vacuole** (mentioned in option 2) is a storage sac found in cells. In **plant cells**, it is typically very large and surrounded by a **single membrane** called the **tonoplast**. Its function is primarily related to **osmoregulation** and **storage**, not genetic control.
 
 
 
• **Cell Types lacking a Nucleus:**
 
 
• While most eukaryotic cells are **nucleated**, certain mature cells like **human Red Blood Cells (RBCs)** and **sieve tube cells** in **vascular plants** lack a nucleus to optimize their specific **functions**, such as carrying **oxygen** or transporting **nutrients**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Genetic Function:** The nucleus stores **hereditary information** in the form of **genes**, which are segments of **DNA**. It controls **cell reproduction** (mitosis/meiosis) and **metabolic activities** by directing **protein synthesis** through **transcription**.
 
• **Nuclear Pore Complex (NPC):** The **pores** mentioned in the question are actually complex protein assemblies. A typical mammalian cell nucleus may contain about **3000 to 4000** nuclear pores, facilitating the transport of approximately **1000 molecules per second**.
 
• **Evolutionary Aspect:** The presence of a **double membrane**-bound nucleus is the defining hallmark of **Domain Eukarya**, distinguishing them from **Bacteria** and **Archaea**, which store their **DNA** in a simple **nucleoid** region.
